C-REWORK-CIRCUIT.Summary: Extend C-ESCALATION-HONESTY with a cross-window ceiling: the first in-window breaker fire (trigger R or D) stays paused-pending-approval with an auditable --reason resume; the second in-window breaker fire on the same task enters a new terminal cursor state that refuses resume. Governance is untouched — spec and plan keep their status. A human still supersedes if the bundle is to die. Churn figures are evidence on the escalation, never a trip condition.
C-REWORK-CIRCUIT.Problem:
C-ESCALATION-HONESTY already stops a window: trigger R fires on two fails of the same FailureSignature (exact kind + key), trigger D on four distinct signatures, and the next attempt is hard-refused with gate.attempt.escalated. What that bundle cannot see, by construction, is a loop that crosses windows. windowStart = lastResolvingResumeId (src/grace-cursor.ts:1709, :1721): every escalation-clearing resume restarts both counters. Escalate → resume --reason → escalate → resume repeats without bound, and a signature that recurs across windows is invisible to a window-scoped counter.
Measured 2026-09-02 at HEAD e5aced5664b389f68caf791baf034a4b01ad0444 (F142's probe class, by reading the live functions, not by restating the finding): CursorState is absent | idle | in-progress | paused | paused-pending-approval | complete | discarded. KNOWN_KIND_STATE maps escalation → paused-pending-approval and resume → in-progress. ESCALATION_RESOLVER_KINDS is the singleton set {"resume"}. FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2. FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4. There is no third constant, no cross-window counter, and no cursor state that means "resume will not clear this".
D24 (2026-09-02, maintainer, variant A of three) charters this bundle: a cross-window recurrence detector and a global cap; on trip, a terminal escalation state that refuses resume. Variant B (auto-supersede) was rejected because supersede must name a replacement, and an auto-generated successor is a governance artifact no human authored. Variant C (report only) was rejected because it stops nothing. This spec implements A and does not reintroduce B: it must not write status onto spec.xml or plan.xml.
F144 (2026-09-02) measured that file-rewrite depth does not discriminate a failing bundle from a shipping one, and the corpus holds no positive example of the failure a churn ceiling would detect. Re-measured 2026-09-02 at this HEAD (File path is element text, digest is the only attribute; .ngrace/ excluded; rewrite = digest differs from the previous recorded digest of that path). 54 run-ledger.xml files under .ngrace/changes; 42 bundles carry attempt events (40 applied, 2 superseded). Mean deepest-file rewrite count 2.33 applied / 3.00 superseded. The six deepest are all applied: C-FINDING-SEVERITIES 7/4, C-BUNDLE-BASE-REF 5/3, C-DRIFT-HONESTY 5/2, C-ESCALATION-HONESTY 5/2, C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE 5/3, C-TEACHING-SURFACE 5/11. F144's 41 / 39 / 2.38 have aged by one applied bundle; the six named rows still hold. The ruling F144 yields: churn is the payload, recurrence is the trigger. Churn must not be the trip condition at any threshold this corpus can justify.

Goals.Goal: Keep C-ESCALATION-HONESTY intact for the ordinary first escalation. Trigger R (2 same-signature fails in the current window) and trigger D (4 distinct failing signatures in the current window), evaluated R before D, still write kind escalation, still enter paused-pending-approval, still say the task has not failed, and still clear on a non-empty --reason resume. That bundle's window rule, signature equality (exact kind and exact key), and "passes never escalate" all survive. This extends that ruling; it does not overturn it.

Ship one new named constant FIX_ESCALATION_CEILING = 2 beside FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET and FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET. Unit: escalations per task, counting kind=escalation plus kind=circuit events for that task across the whole accounting stream (not the current window). When an in-window R or D decision would fire and that count is already >= 1, write kind=circuit instead of kind=escalation and enter paused-pending-supersede. The second breaker fire is the proven loop; the first remains the human replan checkpoint.

A circuit-tripped task refuses resume (both ngrace cursor resume and ngrace cursor advance --kind resume) before any write, with a stable coded refuse that names paused-pending-supersede and ngrace supersede as the exit. Resume must not resolve circuit: ESCALATION_RESOLVER_KINDS stays the singleton {"resume"} and continues to resolve only ordinary escalation. Further attempts on that task stay refused. Spec.xml and plan.xml status are not written. The only exit that ends the stuck task is human supersede of the bundle.

Attach file-level churn evidence to both the ordinary first escalation and the circuit trip, computed from WriteEvidence the ledger already holds (path as File element text, digest as the only File attribute; F141). The message names which files were rewritten how many times across how many windows, and which signatures recurred across windows when any did. Churn is never consulted as a trip predicate.

The live-constant substring helper fixBudgetSkillRequiredSubstrings gains a third entry built from FIX_ESCALATION_CEILING so prose and code cannot diverge on the ceiling, the same way they cannot diverge on R=2 and D=4.

CursorState gains paused-pending-supersede. Detecting a cycle as a repeated sequence of signatures, or as a WriteEvidence digest-set returning after diverging. Owner: this spec's cycle decision. Sequence detection punishes a confused agent that invents new keys (the case trigger D already bounds in-window) and misses the named gap (the same signature across windows). A digest-set cycle can only see path plus sha256 (F141) and F144 shows rewriting the same files is what shipping work looks like. The honest cycle is the in-window breaker firing a second time.

A first-reappearance trip: fail(A) in window 2 after window 1 already escalated on A. Owner: F9.8 / C-ESCALATION-HONESTY. After a documented replan, one fail of the same signature is honest red-first of the new approach, not a proven loop. The loop is the in-window breaker firing again.

A bundle-level ceiling (trip when any N tasks in the bundle have escalated, or when the bundle's tasks each loop once as a single bundle trip). Owner: this spec's grain decision. The existing R/D budget is per task; changing the grain would punish a five-task plan whose tasks each take one ordinary replan. A task that loops twice trips that task; siblings may continue; supersede of the bundle remains the exit if that task is required.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FIRST-ESCALATION-UNCHANGED: Under a fresh budget window, the C-ESCALATION-HONESTY sequence table still holds for the first breaker fire. fail(A), fail(A) writes kind=escalation, state paused-pending-approval, trigger R, and the message still says the task has not failed / replan decision is owed. fail(A,B,C,D) writes ordinary escalation, trigger D. --reason resume still clears that task, opens a new window, and returns in-progress when no other task is stuck. Spec.xml and plan.xml status are unchanged. Failure conditions: first R or D writes circuit; first escalation refuses resume; message claims the task failed; status on spec or plan is written.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CEILING-TRIPS-ON-SECOND: FIX_ESCALATION_CEILING = 2, counting kind=escalation plus kind=circuit events per task across the accounting stream. After ordinary R (or D) and a reason-bearing resume, the next in-window R (or D) writes kind=circuit, not escalation; CursorState is paused-pending-supersede; KNOWN_KIND_STATE maps circuit to that state. Unrecognized kinds still do not resolve to in-progress. KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS length pin is 11 and includes circuit. Failure conditions: second breaker fire writes escalation again; ceiling is 3; count is windows or signature recurrences only, so a second D with new keys never trips; circuit maps to paused-pending-approval or discarded; unknown kind becomes in-progress.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RED-FIRST-AFTER-RESUME: After ordinary escalation on A and a reason-bearing resume, a single fail(A) in the new window does not escalate and does not trip the circuit. A second fail(A) in that window does trip the circuit. Failure conditions: first reappearance of A after resume writes circuit (punishes F9.8 red-first); second fail(A) in the new window only writes another ordinary escalation.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RESUME-REFUSES-CIRCUIT: When a task is circuit-tripped, ngrace cursor resume and ngrace cursor advance --kind resume for that task refuse with a non-zero exit / GraceCommandError before writing a resume event, without clearing the circuit set, and without writing spec or plan status. The refuse names paused-pending-supersede and ngrace supersede as the exit. It must not tell the operator to pass --reason and continue. Ordinary resume (task not escalated and not circuit-tripped) still works without --reason. Escalation-clearing resume on a still-ordinary paused-pending-approval task still requires --reason. Failure conditions: resume writes; circuit cleared; message advises --reason continue; only one of the two entry paths enforces; ordinary pause/resume broken.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-REFUSES-CIRCUIT: Further attempts on a circuit-tripped task are refused. evaluateAttemptGate (or the sibling that receives the circuit set) refuses with gate.attempt.circuit-tripped, which is registered in GATE_CATALOG, and whose remediation names supersede, not resume. recordAttempt refuses the same tasks. Reusing gate.attempt.escalated for this case fails the criterion (that code's remediation currently says resume). Failure conditions: attempts accepted; gate permits and recordAttempt refuses (or the reverse); catalog missing; remediation says resume.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PER-TASK-GRAIN: Circuit is per task. T-001 circuit-tripped does not prevent T-002 from recording attempts in T-002's own window, and does not prevent T-002 from a reason-bearing resume of T-002's own ordinary escalation. Bundle-level state is paused-pending-supersede while any task is circuit-tripped. Failure conditions: one task's circuit freezes sibling attempts; bundle state stays paused-pending-approval while a circuit-tripped task exists.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHURN-IS-PAYLOAD: Ordinary first escalation and circuit trip both carry file-level churn in the user-visible message: each non-.ngrace/ WriteEvidence path (File element text) with a content digest, how many times that digest differed from the previous recorded digest of that path on this task's attempts in id order, and how many budget windows those attempts spanned. Circuit also names which FailureSignatures (kind:key) appeared in two or more windows, or that none did when the ceiling tripped on distinct-signature escalations. Changing rewrite counts without a second in-window R or D must not trip. Unavailable WriteEvidence is omitted, not invented. Failure conditions: churn consulted as a predicate; message omits paths or counts on a trip that has available evidence; .ngrace/ paths listed as product churn; bytes or lines claimed (F141: not derivable).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-GOVERNANCE-WRITE: On circuit trip, spec.xml and plan.xml status attributes are byte-identical to before the fail that tripped. No Replacement is written. ngrace supersede remains a human act and still requires --replacement. Failure conditions: status becomes superseded; a successor bundle is created; Replacement is authored by the breaker.

Assumptions.Assumption: Cycle definition (open question 1). A cycle is the in-window breaker (trigger R or D) firing a second time on the same task — equivalently, a FailureSignature appearing in two windows only as evidence, not as an earlier trip. Rejected: repeated signature sequence (overfits; confused agents invent keys; misses the named cross-window gap). Rejected: WriteEvidence digest-set returning after diverging (F141 limits visibility to path+sha256; F144 shows rewrite of the same files is shipping work). Rejected: first reappearance of a prior-window signature after resume (F9.8: that fail is honest red-first of the replan).

Cap and unit (open question 2). Constant FIX_ESCALATION_CEILING = 2, counting escalations per task (kind=escalation plus kind=circuit on that task, whole stream). Why this unit: each ordinary escalation is the human-visible checkpoint that already required a --reason resume; the second checkpoint is the proven loop. Why 2: measured 2026-09-02 across every archived run-ledger.xml, 8 tasks have ever escalated, each exactly once, each with a matching resume; max escalations on one task = 1; tasks with 2+ = 0. N=2 therefore has no false positive in this corpus and is the minimum that preserves the first C-ESCALATION-HONESTY checkpoint. N=3 would allow two failed replans with no positive example to calibrate against. Rejected: counting windows (windows = escalations + 1, off-by-one vs the checkpoint the human already paid). Rejected: counting recurrences of one signature as the only unit (misses the D-loop: four new keys, resume, four new keys). Recurrence of one signature across windows is the detector's evidence payload on the same trip, not a second threshold.

State and exit (open question 3). New CursorState paused-pending-supersede, new event kind circuit, cleared only by human ngrace supersede of the bundle. ESCALATION_RESOLVER_KINDS stays {"resume"} and does not resolve circuit. Existing union members cannot say this honestly (D21): paused-pending-approval is resume-cleared by definition; discarded claims supersede already happened; complete is a completion judgment. No new operator verb.

Grain (open question 4). Per task, matching the existing budget. A bundle whose tasks each take one ordinary replan must not trip. A bundle whose tasks each loop (two escalations each) trips each looping task individually; that is already N circuit states, and supersede of the bundle is still the exit if those tasks are required. Sibling progress is information, not a leak.

Churn evidence (open question 5). Computed from WriteEvidence already on attempt events: walk the task's attempts in id order; for each File whose path (element text) is not under .ngrace/ and whose digest attribute is a content digest, if that digest differs from the previous recorded digest of that path, count a rewrite. Present in the message, sorted by rewrite count descending, with window count and recurring signatures. Attached to ordinary first escalation (this-window churn, to inform the replan) and to circuit (cross-window totals). Never a trip predicate. F144's six applied deepest-churn bundles, re-measured 2026-09-02, would all have been invalidated by a "3 files × 5 rewrites" ceiling; that is why this spec forbids that ceiling.
